value.gesture: arms in a big circle: hug the world

story_world: Gan Eden and the newly created world: lush soft green hills, a clear sparkling river, fruit trees heavy with fruit, bright flowers, gentle friendly animals, wide open sky and warm luminous golden light. Pre-civilization: no buildings, no houses, no fences, no tools, no modern objects. Adam and Chava wear simple, modest, full-coverage tunics. Hashem is never shown as a figure, only as light.

cards.image_prompt:
The very first moment of creation: a soft, velvety deep-blue darkness over a calm, still sea, and
right in the middle a brilliant burst of warm golden light breaking through, its rays spreading out in
every direction like a sunrise opening. Tiny sparkles of light dance on the water below and the first
glow touches the gentle waves. No sun disc, no figure, only pure radiant light. The darkness feels
quiet and cozy, not scary, and the light feels like a wonderful surprise. WOW, LIGHT!

back.objective: Hashem made a beautiful world for us
back.say:
**At the very beginning, there was nothing at all. Just dark.** [Everyone cover your eyes]
**Then Hashem said, "Let there be light!"** [Open your eyes: WOW!]
**This week we'll see everything Hashem made.**

ask.text: What do you see in this picture?
What do you think Hashem made next?

back.transition: What did Hashem make on Day 1?

pshat.text: The Torah opens: "In the beginning Hashem created the heavens and the earth." The earth was empty and dark, with water everywhere. Then Hashem said, "Let there be light," and there was light. Hashem saw that the light was good (טוֹב), and separated light from dark: day and night. That was Day 1.

sages.text: Rashi teaches that the Torah begins with the story of creation to show that the whole world belongs to Hashem, who made it. That is why we take care of it: it is Hashem's world, lent to us.

hard_questions.answer: The dark is just the time before the light. Hashem made the light, and Hashem made the night too, so we can rest.
hard_questions.redirect: Let's cover our eyes and open them again: WOW, light!

hard_questions.answer: Nobody made Hashem. Hashem was always here, before everything, and made everything else. That's a big question, and grown-ups wonder about it too!
hard_questions.redirect: What is your favorite thing Hashem made?

adapt.see: Dim the classroom lights during 'just dark', then switch them on at 'Let there be light!'
adapt.do: Children who don't want to cover their eyes can cup their hands into a tiny 'dark cave' instead.
adapt.join: Everyone can say WOW together, or show WOW with a big open-mouth face and jazz hands.

guide.extend: Light walk: turn off the lights and let each child point a flashlight at one thing in the room and name it.
guide.tip: Practice the hug-the-world gesture (arms in a big circle) for this week's value, 'caring for Hashem's world', and use it every day.

cards.image_prompt:
Adam (oatmeal tunic, short curly dark hair and beard) kneels in the lush garden, chest-up and close,
gently cupping a handful of rich brown earth with a tiny green sprout in it, looking down at it with a
proud, caring smile. Behind him: bright flowers, a fruit tree, soft green hills and a sparkling river
under a warm sky glowing with morning light. A friendly rabbit peeks at the sprout beside his elbow.
Gentle, warm and proud: the first gardener.

back.objective: Adam's job: take care of the garden
back.say:
[Point to Adam] **This is Adam, the very first person!**
**Hashem made Adam from the earth** [Scoop up pretend dirt]
**and gave him a big job: take care of the garden.** [Water the plants!]

ask.text: Show me how you'd water a flower!

hebrew.gesture: cup your hands, scoop the earth

pshat.text: Hashem formed Adam from the dust of the ground (אֲדָמָה, adamah: that's where his name comes from) and breathed the breath of life into him. Then Hashem put Adam in Gan Eden "to work it and to guard it" (לְעָבְדָהּ וּלְשָׁמְרָהּ): the very first job in the world was taking care of the garden.

sages.text: Our Sages teach that Hashem took Adam around all the trees of Gan Eden and said: 'See how beautiful My world is. I made it all for you. Take care not to spoil it, because nobody will come after you to fix it.'

adapt.see: Bring a small pot of real soil so children can see and touch 'adamah'.
adapt.do: Children can scoop with one hand, or pretend-water with a cup, instead of the two-hand scoop.
adapt.join: Point to Adam on the card, or point to something in the picture Adam takes care of.

guide.extend: Plant a seed in a clear cup of soil. Each day this week, a different child is the 'Adam' who waters it.
guide.tip: Say אָדָם and אֲדָמָה side by side, slowly, so children hear the shared sound; let them guess why.

cards.image_prompt:
Chava, a grown-up young woman (sage-green long-sleeved dress, long dark wavy hair loosely tied back),
chest-up portrait in the garden, smiling warmly and kindly. She holds up her open hands to offer a
small bird a few seeds; the little bluebird hops onto her fingertips. Behind her: flowering bushes,
fruit trees and a clear river in soft golden light, with a wide pale sky above. Friendly, warm and
helpful: a helping hand.

back.objective: Adam and Chava help each other
back.say:
**Adam was alone. Hashem said, "It is not good to be alone."** [Sad face…]
**So Hashem made Chava!** […happy face!]
**Now Adam and Chava could help each other take care of the garden.** [High-five a friend]

hebrew.gesture: hook your pinkies with a friend

pshat.text: Hashem said, "It is not good for the man to be alone; I will make a helper for him." Hashem let Adam sleep and made Chava from a part of Adam's side, then brought her to Adam, and Adam was glad. Later Adam named her Chava (חַוָּה), "because she was the mother of all living things." On the card we say only "Hashem made Chava" (sensitivity reframe); the side detail is here if a child asks.

sages.text: Our Sages teach that Hashem began all people with just one person, to teach that every single person is as precious as a whole world.

hard_questions.answer: The Torah says Hashem let Adam fall asleep and made Chava from a part of Adam's side, so they would always be close, like a team. It didn't hurt.
hard_questions.redirect: Who is on your team at home?

adapt.see: Show the sad face and the happy face with two simple drawn faces held up in turn.
adapt.do: A child who doesn't want to high-five can give a thumbs up or a wave to a friend instead.
adapt.join: Children can hook pinkies with the teacher, or point to a friend who helps them.

guide.extend: Helping hands: children trace a hand on paper and the teacher writes one way they helped someone today.
guide.tip: Keep the 'alone' beat short and light; move quickly to the happy face so nobody feels sad for long.

cards.image_prompt:
A brand-new world on its third day, wide view: golden light pours over everything from a glowing
sky. A wide blue sky above, a calm sparkling sea on one side, and on the other side fresh green hills
of dry land where the very first trees, grass and bright flowers are sprouting and unfurling. A river
winds from the hills down to the sea. No animals and no people yet: everything is fresh, clean and
brand new, glistening like morning dew. Wonder and freshness everywhere!

back.objective: Days 1–3: light, sky, land and plants
back.say:
**Day 1: light!** [Open hands wide] **Day 2: the sky up high** [Reach up!] **and water down low.** [Wiggle like waves]
**Day 3: dry land, with trees and flowers!** [Grow like a tree]
**And Hashem saw it was… TOV!** [Thumbs up!]

ask.text: Show me how a tree grows!

hebrew.gesture: fists, then open wide like a sunburst

back.transition: But the sky was still empty…

pshat.text: Day 1: Hashem made light and separated it from the dark. Day 2: Hashem made the sky (רָקִיעַ, a dome) between the water above and the water below. Day 3: the water gathered together so dry land appeared, land and seas, and the earth sprouted grass, plants and fruit trees. After the light, the land and seas, and the plants, "Hashem saw that it was good" (כִּי־טוֹב).

adapt.see: Point to the light, the sky, the water and the trees in the picture as you say each day.
adapt.do: Seated children can do every movement with arms only: open hands, reach up, wave arms, branch arms.
adapt.join: Everyone joins the 'TOV!' thumbs up at the end, with or without words.

guide.extend: Make a 3-panel 'Days 1-3' strip: yellow (light), blue (sky and water), green (land and trees).
guide.tip: Hold up 1, 2, 3 fingers for each day; the counting carries into Story 2 and the 7 TOVs.

cards.image_prompt:
The very same landscape as the earlier card, the same hills, river, sea and trees, now FULL OF LIFE:
a smiling warm sun shines in the sky with a pale crescent moon and a few twinkly stars still visible
at one side; colorful fish leap out of the sea and a friendly whale splashes far out; birds swoop over
the hills; gentle animals fill the green land: a giraffe, an elephant, a deer, a rabbit, a lion cub
and a family of ducks by the river. Joyful and busy, the whole world bursting with life!

back.objective: Days 4–6: sky lights, fish, birds, animals, people
back.say:
**Day 4: the sun, the moon, and twinkly stars!** [Twinkle fingers]
**Day 5: fish that swim** [Swim hands] **and birds that fly!** [Flap!]
**Day 6: animals and people!** [Your favorite animal sound]
**And Hashem saw it was… TOV!** [Thumbs up!]
back.transition: Who will take care of it all?

pshat.text: Day 4: Hashem made the two great lights, the sun for the day and the moon for the night, and the stars. Day 5: the water filled with fish and great sea creatures, and birds flew across the sky; Hashem blessed them. Day 6: Hashem made every kind of land animal, and then people. Hashem saw everything and it was "very good" (טוֹב מְאֹד). Point out that the picture is the same place as Story 1, now full of life.

hard_questions.answer: The Torah says Hashem made every kind of animal, the giant ones and the tiny ones. Dinosaurs lived a very, very long time ago, and Hashem made them too.
hard_questions.redirect: Show me a giant dinosaur step, and now a tiny ant step!

adapt.see: Lay the Story 1 card next to this one: what is new in the picture?
adapt.do: Children can choose any movement for their animal: a hop, a stomp, a slither on the hands.
adapt.join: Children who don't want to make a sound can show their animal with hands or point to it on the card.

guide.extend: Sorting game: sky, water or land? Children sort animal pictures (or toy animals) into three hoops.
guide.tip: Keep the animal sounds short: count down 3-2-1 and finish together with the TOV thumbs up.

cards.image_prompt:
The same garden world at rest on the seventh day, a calm golden evening: soft peach and gold light
glows across the sky and over the still river. The animals are resting peacefully: a lion cub curled
up asleep beside a lamb, birds tucked quietly in a tree, a deer lying in the soft grass, ducks floating
gently. The flowers are closed and the trees stand still. Everything is quiet, cozy and peaceful, a
warm feeling of rest. SHHH... it is a special day.

back.objective: Hashem rested and made Shabbat special
back.say:
**Hashem made the whole world in six days.** [Count fingers: 1… 6!]
**On the seventh day, Hashem rested.** [Head on hands, shhh…]
**Hashem made that day special. We call it… Shabbat!** [Light pretend candles]

ask.text: What did Hashem do on day 7?

pshat.text: The heavens and the earth were finished. On the seventh day Hashem finished the work and rested (וַיִּשְׁבֹּת, vayishbot, the root of "Shabbat"). Hashem blessed the seventh day and made it holy.

hard_questions.answer: Hashem never gets tired. Hashem stopped making new things to show us that one day each week is for resting and enjoying the world.
hard_questions.redirect: What do you like to do on Shabbat?

adapt.see: Show two real (unlit) Shabbat candlesticks, or a picture of them.
adapt.do: Children who can't sit still can 'rest' by sitting cross-legged with hands in lap.
adapt.join: Everyone can join a whispered 'Shabbat Shalom' or wave to the class.

guide.extend: Rest and notice: one minute of quiet with eyes closed, then each child names one sound they heard.
guide.tip: Teach this card on Friday (Day 5 of the week plan) so it leads straight into the real Shabbat.

cards.image_prompt:
Adam (oatmeal tunic, curly dark hair and beard) stands in a sunny meadow of the garden with one hand
stretched out and pointing gently at a big friendly lion with a fluffy golden mane, smiling as he names
it. The lion sits proudly and looks up at him happily. Other friendly animals wait their turn in a
cheerful line: a giraffe, a zebra, a little lamb, a bunny, and colorful parrots and a dove fluttering at
shoulder height. Chava (sage-green long dress) kneels nearby, gently petting a little lamb and laughing.
Green hills and leafy trees behind them, warm light. Delighted and caring: YOU ARE A LION!

back.say:
**Hashem brought all the animals to Adam,** [Point to the animals]
**and Adam gave each one a name! "You are a LION!"** [Roar!] **"You are a BIRD!"** [Tweet!]
**Adam's job was to take care of them all.**

ask.text: What name would you give this animal?

back.transition: How can WE take care of the world?

pshat.text: Hashem brought every animal of the field and every bird of the sky to Adam "to see what he would call them", and whatever Adam called each one, that became its name. Adam was put in the garden to work it and to guard it. The snake, the tree and the fruit (Genesis 3) are NOT on any card: if a child asks, use the scripted answers below.

sages.text: Our Sages teach that Hashem showed Adam the whole garden and asked him to take care not to ruin it. Naming the animals was part of caring for them: you look closely at each one.

hard_questions.q: Did they eat the fruit? What about the snake?
hard_questions.answer: Hashem asked Adam and Chava not to eat from one special tree. The snake tricked them, and they ate it: they made a mistake. Hashem still took care of them and even made them clothes.
hard_questions.redirect: What can we do when we make a mistake? (Say sorry, try again.)

hard_questions.q: Did Adam and Chava have to leave the garden?
hard_questions.answer: Yes, after the mistake they went to live outside the garden. Hashem gave them clothes and stayed with them, and they kept working the land.
hard_questions.redirect: How can we take care of the world right here?

adapt.see: Hold up toy animals (or pictures) one at a time for children to name.
adapt.do: Use a soft roar and a quiet tweet; children can show the animal with hands instead of sound.
adapt.join: Point to an animal on the card, or hold the toy animal while a friend names it.

guide.extend: Name-it circle: pass a toy animal around; each child gives it a new silly name and one way to take care of it.
guide.tip: If a child mentions the snake or the fruit, answer calmly with the script below, then come back to the animals.

cards.image_prompt:
A sunny gan (Jewish preschool) garden corner in the afternoon. Five children ages 4-5 care for plants
and animals together: an Ethiopian girl in a yellow dress tips a small watering can over a pot of red
flowers; a Sephardi boy with a kippah plants a seedling in a raised bed, hands in the soil; an Ashkenazi
girl with red curls and a purple skirt holds up a seed feeder while a little bird lands on it; a
Mizrahi boy with a kippah gently holds a pet rabbit on his lap; a fair-haired boy with a kippah carries
a basket of fallen leaves, grinning at his friends. A teacher in a knee-length skirt kneels and smiles.
Leafy trees, a painted fence of flower pots and a sunny sky. Proud, happy and busy helping!

back.objective: Each child names one way to help
back.say:
**Adam took care of the garden. We can take care of Hashem's world too!**
[Share one way you do it]
**How can YOU take care of the world?** [Pass the card to whoever is sharing]

ask.text: What could you do for a plant or an animal?

pshat.text: Hashem put Adam in Gan Eden "to work it and to guard it" (לְעָבְדָהּ וּלְשָׁמְרָהּ). The word on this card, שׁוֹמְרִים (shomrim, "guarding, taking care"), comes from that verse: we are the guardians of Hashem's world today.

sages.text: Our Sages teach that Hashem told Adam: 'Take care not to spoil My world, because there is no one to fix it after you.'

adapt.see: Show 3 picture cues (watering can, bird feeder, recycling bin) for children who need an idea.
adapt.do: Children can act out their idea (watering, sweeping, feeding) instead of saying it.
adapt.join: A child can point to one of the picture cues or to a feeling face on the back.

guide.extend: Make a class 'Shomrim' chart: each child's helping idea, with a sticker each time they do it this week.
guide.tip: Use the hug-the-world gesture (arms in a big circle) every time a child shares an idea.

cards.image_prompt:
Adam (oatmeal tunic) and Chava (sage-green long dress) stand side by side on a green hilltop in the
glowing garden, grinning with joy, each giving a big THUMBS UP toward the viewer. All around them the
whole world glows warm and golden: fruit trees, bright flowers, a sparkling river, a rainbow of birds
and a happy lion, deer and rabbits nearby. A radiant warm sky above, light shining on everything.
Everything is GOOD! TOV!

back.objective: Say, show, and use the word "tov"
back.say:
**Our Hebrew word is TOV. It means good!** [Thumbs up!]
**Every time Hashem made something, Hashem saw it was… TOV!**
**Let's count 7 TOVs!** [Count on fingers: tov, tov, tov…]

ask.text: What is something tov in our classroom?

pshat.text: After making the light, the land and seas, the plants, the sun and moon, the fish and birds, and the land animals, "Hashem saw that it was good" (כִּי־טוֹב). At the very end Hashem saw everything and it was "very good" (טוֹב מְאֹד). That is 7 TOVs in the creation story.

adapt.see: Write טוֹב big on the board and point to it each time the class says TOV.
adapt.do: Children who can't make a thumbs up can nod or smile big for TOV.
adapt.join: Everyone shows the thumbs up together; no words needed.

guide.extend: Tov hunt: children find 7 good things in the room and give each one a TOV thumbs up.
guide.tip: Review this week's words: אוֹר (OR, light) and שַׁבָּת (sha-BAT). Say each, then TOV!

cards.image_prompt:
No art: the home card front is drawn by the Card Designer (a family waters a plant before Shabbat in
the try-at-home activity). Never generated.

back.objective: We learned about **caring for Hashem's world**

shabbat_question.en: "What is your favorite thing Hashem made?"

hebrew.gesture: Ask your child to show you the "tov thumbs"!

try_at_home.text: Go on a "tov walk": find 7 things Hashem made.

pshat.text: This week's parasha, Bereshit, tells how Hashem made the world in six days and rested on the seventh, and how Adam was put in Gan Eden "to work it and to guard it". Families can ask about the 7 days and the TOV thumbs.

adapt.see: Send the card home with a small picture of the TOV thumbs so families know the gesture.
adapt.do: Families who can't walk outside can do the tov walk around the home or from a window.
adapt.join: Non-speaking children can show the tov thumbs at the Shabbat table.

guide.extend: Invite families to send a photo or drawing of their favorite thing Hashem made for a class 'Tov Wall'.
guide.tip: Send the home card on Friday with the family letter (guide p.15).
